Confirmado el patrón: mismo caso que `load.ts` (`restoreSessionStateFromLog` sobre `AppStateLike`, `setAppState` concreto sobre `AppState`). Propongo las dos ediciones: importar el tipo `AppState` vía el shim de `appStateHooks.js` (ya usado en el archivo) y envolver la llamada en el borde.

```json
{"module": "pattern:app-state-like-callback-boundary",
 "edits": [
   {"file": "src/packages/repl/src/screens/REPLView.tsx",
    "old_string": "import { useAppState } from '../appStateHooks.js';",
    "new_string": "import { useAppState, type AppState } from '../appStateHooks.js';",
    "replace_all": false},
   {"file": "src/packages/repl/src/screens/REPLView.tsx",
    "old_string": "        // Restore file history and attribution state from the resumed conversation\n        restoreSessionStateFromLog(log, setAppState);",
    "new_string": "        // Restore file history and attribution state from the resumed conversation\n        // restoreSessionStateFromLog opera sobre AppStateLike (contrato\n        // estructural que storage usa para no importar el AppState real);\n        // se adapta al setAppState concreto en el borde de la llamada.\n        restoreSessionStateFromLog(log, update =>\n          setAppState(prev => update(prev) as AppState),\n        );",
    "replace_all": false}
```
